Put a living 3D agent on your website in 30 seconds.

Two lines of HTML. No build step, no npm install.

Paste, refresh, and a 3D character is standing in the corner of your page, greeting visitors and answering questions.

As easy as embedding a video.

three.ws/tutorials/embed-in-30-seconds

How it works:

Build your agent at three.ws/create. Pick a character, give it a name and a personality.

Copy its ID into the two lines, and refresh your page.

It animates, greets and chats out of the box. Works in plain HTML, React and Next.js.

issues.problem: The image footer states 'No build step · no npm install · free and open source'. Nothing in the verification results or the live page text quoted by a passing check supports 'free and open source'. A claim that appears only inside the image is still a claim, and it is unverified.
issues.fix: Recapture the card with the footer reading 'No build step · no npm install' only, or keep 'free and open source' only if a passing check verifies it (e.g. a probes/docs page stating the embed runtime is open source).

issues.problem: 'Living' is an adjective, not a mechanism; the same post already proves the claim with 'Two lines of HTML', which is stronger.
issues.fix: Replace with 'Put a 3D agent on your website in 30 seconds.' The mechanism carries the line on its own.

issues.quote: As easy as embedding a video.
issues.problem: A standalone simile line drifts toward copywriting; the measurable fact (two lines, no build step) is already stated.
issues.fix: Drop the line or fold it into the prior sentence as 'Paste, refresh, and a 3D character is standing in the corner of your page, greeting visitors and answering questions.' The post survives without it.
